review_model_policy.name: codex-blocker-gate-sonnet-final-v1
review_model_policy.description: Every exact head begins with logical Codex reviewer lanes and a fresh logical Codex verifier, all executed as independent read-only Claude Code CLI invocations. A deterministic, persisted checkpoint admits Opus only when the canonical validated blocker count is zero after policy application and complete prior-finding revalidation. Blockers produce a preliminary Codex-only REQUEST_CHANGES review and defer Opus. Zero blockers admit Opus and produce a combined final review. Persisted Sonnet-named policy identifiers, checkpoint/state keys, labels, and API fields remain compatibility aliases for this Opus phase. Logical agent identity, execution harness, auth, and exact backend model are recorded separately.

verifier.fallback_when: Opus reviewer evidence exists but the primary Opus verifier fails or is unparseable

preliminary.title: Preliminary review — Codex only
preliminary.sonnet: Opus not run (deferred by blocker gate; field name retained for compatibility)

review_model_policy.provenance_rule: Persist exact head, phase, decision, canonical blocker count, reviewer and verifier attempt IDs/logical agents/exact backend models/harnesses/auth/roles/PIDs/exit statuses/artifacts/status/parseability, prior-finding revalidation, deterministic policy result, Opus coverage range, Opus last-reviewed SHA through the persisted Sonnet-named compatibility fields, publication IDs, and fallback reason after every checkpoint. Logical agent compatibility identity and Claude Code execution identity must remain separate.

specialists.description: Deep security analysis: cryptographic implementations, consensus safety, proof system soundness, race conditions in concurrent code, web/DOM injection, remote dependency boundaries, trust boundary violations, unsafe operations, timing attacks

Rust quality review: error handling discipline (no unwraps in production), architectural patterns, idiomatic Rust usage, proper lifetimes/generics, test structure, performance patterns (unnecessary clones, allocation in hot paths)
FFI and cross-language boundary review: memory safety across Swift/Rust/WASM boundaries, correct ownership transfer, FFI-safe types, panic safety across FFI, WASM binding correctness, ABI stability

Bitcoin Core backport prerequisite verification: compares upstream starting states vs Dash to detect missing intermediate PRs, identifies workarounds masking missing APIs/infrastructure, traces dependency chains. Activated for PRs with 'backport' in title or cherry-picks from bitcoin/bitcoin.

TenderDash (Go) consensus and security review: BFT protocol correctness (propose/prevote/precommit, locking, +2/3 thresholds, double-sign / equivocation), validator set + LLMQ quorum signature verification (BLS threshold sigs, quorum hash binding, chain-id and domain separation), vote/commit/block/header validation, evidence handling, light client safety, ABCI app-vs-consensus trust boundary, RPC and P2P input validation, DoS / resource exhaustion (unbounded allocations, slow peers, mempool flooding), Go concurrency (data races, deadlocks, goroutine leaks), nondeterminism in consensus-critical paths.

Dash Core commit-history hygiene review (no code correctness). Dashpay/dash merges PR commits into develop without squashing, so the ordered stack lands in permanent history. Flags fixup/wip/no-op commits, obviously separate commits that should be squashed, misleading commit messages, mixed unrelated changes in a single commit visible from per-commit stats, and merge/rebase noise — while leaving legitimate multi-commit stacks (refactor+feature+tests, backport/cherry-pick series, justified mechanical follow-ups) alone.
